sections.h2: Where is Newton, Massachusetts, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Newton is a city in Middlesex County about 8 miles west of downtown Boston, and it is a patchwork of thirteen villages instead of one center. It borders Boston's Brighton and West Roxbury neighborhoods, Brookline, Watertown, Waltham, Weston, Wellesley and Needham.

The city covers 18.16 square miles. The 2020 census counted 88,923 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 90,741. The Charles River runs along the north and west sides, Route 128 passes through the western edge, and the Mass Pike crosses the more urban northern section.

Wikipedia notes that Newton grew around seven hills: Nonantum, Waban, Chestnut Hill, Bald Pate, Oak Hill, Institution Hill and Mount Ida. Slope and elevation change from one village to the next, which affects drainage, basements and how a house sits on its lot.

Newton's villages have no legal borders, but each has its own small center and its own name in addresses. Wikipedia lists them as follows.

  • Auburndale and West Newton
  • Chestnut Hill and Waban
  • Newton Centre, Newton Corner and Newton Highlands
  • Newton Lower Falls and Newton Upper Falls, both on the Charles River and both former small industrial sites
  • Newtonville and Nonantum, which is also called Silver Lake or the Lake
  • Oak Hill and Thompsonville

The city uses eleven ZIP codes, from 02458 through 02468 and 02495 for Nonantum. Since village names are not city boundaries, a listing or a deed may carry a different name than a neighbor's mailing address, so confirm the parcel details with the assessor.

Newton was first part of Cambridge, which was settled as the "newe towne" in 1630. English settlement of the Newton area began in 1639, the town was incorporated as Cambridge Village on December 15, 1681, and it took the name Newton in 1766.

It became a city on January 5, 1874. The Boston and Worcester railroad reached West Newton in 1834, and wealthy Boston businessmen built houses on former farmland along the line and on Commonwealth Avenue. Streetcar lines and then automobiles brought later waves of building, and Oak Hill stayed farmland until the 1950s. Mills at Newton Upper Falls and Lower Falls made snuff, chocolate, glue and paper, and the Stanley Motor Carriage Company, maker of the Stanley Steamer, was based here from 1902.

sections.h2: How do people travel around Newton?
sections.html:
Newton is served by the MBTA's light rail, commuter rail and buses, and by the Mass Pike. The Green Line D branch, also called the Riverside branch, runs through the center of the city to Newton Lower Falls, and Wikipedia puts the ride to downtown Boston at 10 to 30 minutes.

  • Green Line B branch ends across from Boston College on Commonwealth Avenue.
  • Worcester commuter rail serves the northern villages near Waltham.
  • Express buses run to downtown Boston along the Mass Pike.
  • Route 9, Route 30 (Commonwealth Avenue) and Route 16 run east to west.
  • Newton has no major north-south roads, and nearly every north-south street ends within the city.

Wikipedia also reports that the Newtonville commuter rail station will close in December 2026 for accessibility work and reopen in spring 2029, which is worth knowing if your house is near it.

sections.h2: What do the weather and the Charles River mean for a Newton house?
sections.html:
Newton averages about 53.6 inches of precipitation a year, with a record low of minus 21 degrees in February 1934 and a record high of 101 in August 1975, per Wikipedia's climate data. Winter cold and a wet year-round pattern put steady wear on roofs, chimneys, gutters and basements.

Houses close to the Charles River or to Crystal Lake, a 33-acre natural lake in Newton Centre, can raise drainage and moisture questions in an inspection. Houses on the hills can have grade issues. Disclose any known water history to your attorney before you sign a purchase agreement.

sections.h2: Who are the largest employers, and which schools serve Newton?
sections.html:
Newton's largest employers are Boston College and Newton-Wellesley Hospital, and companies based in the city include TechTarget and CyberArk. Higher education here also includes Lasell University, Hebrew College and William James College.

Newton Public Schools runs 15 elementary schools, four middle schools (Bigelow, Brown, Oak Hill and F.A. Day) and two high schools, Newton North and Newton South. Private options include Fessenden School, Newton Country Day School and Mount Alvernia.

sections.h2: How do Newton property taxes and assessments work?
sections.html:
Newton's Assessing Department sets values and handles abatements, exemptions and excise adjustments, while the Treasury and Collector bills and collects the tax. The FY2026 certified rates are $9.69 per $1,000 residential and $18.06 for commercial, industrial and personal property.

The assessing office is at Newton City Hall, Room 111, 1000 Commonwealth Avenue, Newton Centre. Hours are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., and the phone is 617-796-1160. The city's page lists exemption, deferral and work-off programs, with FY2027 applications due on or before April 1, 2027. See the Newton assessing page for the assessor's database and forms.

sections.h2: What steps come before closing on a Newton house?
sections.html:
A Newton seller needs a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate from the fire department and clear title, and nearly always uses a real estate attorney.

  • The Department of Fire Services says to schedule the inspection as soon as you have a closing date, because the rules depend on the build year and last permit.
  • Replace undated or expired battery alarms with sealed 10-year photoelectric ones that have a hush feature.
  • Deeds are recorded at the county registry of deeds, and the Secretary of the Commonwealth offers an email alert service for new recordings on your property.
  • The state deeds excise is set by Chapter 64D, Section 1, per $500 of price.

Registered land, held through the Land Court, makes up a smaller share of Massachusetts property than recorded land.

sections.h2: What do Newton sellers usually face, and how does a cash sale work?
sections.html:
Newton sellers often own older houses that need updating, or are settling an estate or relocating on a short timeline. An older Newton house may need alarm upgrades and repair work before a mortgage buyer's inspection is satisfied.

A cash sale takes lender approval out of the schedule. The fire certificate, title work and recording still happen. Cash Home Buyers can review a Newton house as it stands, with no obligation to accept an offer.

faqs.q: How many villages are in Newton, MA?
faqs.a: Newton has thirteen villages: Auburndale, Chestnut Hill, Newton Centre, Newton Corner, Newton Highlands, Newton Lower Falls, Newton Upper Falls, Newtonville, Nonantum, Oak Hill, Thompsonville, Waban and West Newton.

faqs.q: What is the Newton residential property tax rate?
faqs.a: The FY2026 certified residential rate is $9.69 per $1,000 of assessed value, and the commercial, industrial and personal property rate is $18.06, per the City of Newton.

faqs.q: Does Newton have a Green Line stop?
faqs.a: Yes. The Green Line D branch runs through the center of Newton to Newton Lower Falls, and the B branch ends at Boston College on the Brighton line.

faqs.q: Do I need a smoke and CO certificate to sell in Newton?
faqs.a: Yes. State rules require a certificate of compliance from the local fire department for a sale or transfer. The fire department charges a fee, so call to schedule.

faqs.q: When is the Newton exemption application deadline?
faqs.a: FY2027 tax-assistance and exemption applications are due on or before April 1, 2027, according to the city's assessing page.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Newton house as is?
faqs.a: Yes, you can sell with repairs undone. The smoke and CO certificate, title work and any tax balances still have to be handled before closing.
